title: claude-autoresume usage/plan_fit.json
description: The plan-fit analytics report at ~/.claude-autoresume/usage/plan_fit.json. Written whole, atomically (tmp + replace), by plan_fit.write_plan_fit on the daemon's hourly analytics lane; read by the widget's PlanFitModel (verdict + cost summary) and GraphModel (cost_series only). Single writer, single-ish reader, no lock. Almost every leaf is nullable: compute() tolerates missing or malformed store files and comes back all-null with a warning rather than raising, so 'the key is present but null' is the normal not-enough-data state and must never be conflated with 'the key is missing'.
x-in-band-version-note: No version field. `generated_at` is the only provenance marker and no reader consumes it - the widget staleness-checks by file mtime instead.

generated_at.description: ISO8601 UTC timestamp of this computation. Written every run; read by nobody.

current_plan.description: The plan the observed utilization series was MEASURED against, from config.json's account.plan. Every tier projection is a rescale relative to this, so getting it wrong scales the whole report by current/actual.

account.description: Echo of config.json's account block, so the widget can decide between percentage bars and dollar budget bars without re-reading config.json.

type.description: 'api' switches the widget to dollar budget bars.

plan.description: Mirrors current_plan; kept for the API-tier comparison ratio.

budget.description: Dollar budget windows. Emitted for EVERY account type - the widget decides whether to surface them. Each period is null when its limit is unconfigured in config.json.

weekly.description: The weekly budget window, or JSON null when no weekly limit is configured. The widget decodes null as 'period unconfigured' and omits the bar entirely.

monthly.description: The monthly budget window, or JSON null when no monthly limit is configured.

cost_series.description: Graph-ready API-equivalent cost. Keys are timestamps so the reader needs no knowledge of the bucketing rules. The two sub-objects use DIFFERENT key formats - see each.

hourly.description: UTC hour-bucket ISO8601 timestamp (e.g. '2026-07-18T04:00:00+00:00') -> USD, rounded to 4dp. Pruned to a rolling ~35-day window; covers the widget's 24h / 7d / 1mo graph ranges.

daily.description: UTC date 'YYYY-MM-DD' -> USD, rounded to 2dp. Retained forever; backs the 3mo graph range. The differing key format is why GraphModel carries a dedicated dailyKeyDate helper and a locale-fixed formatter.

moving_averages.description: Dollars/day per window. The denominator is REAL elapsed time (fractional days from max(window start, first data point) to now), not the count of calendar days touched - day-counting quantized 1.33 days of history up to '2 covered days' and deflated the rate ~35%.

value_usd_per_month.description: Null when no window has any data yet.

basis.description: Which moving-average window the run rate was extrapolated from. Prefers 7d, then falls back 90d -> 30d -> 1d. Null when none had data.

cost_peaks.description: Worst observed spend bursts, in API-equivalent dollars.

utilization_observed.description: Peak and weighted-average utilization percentages ACTUALLY observed on the current plan, merged across the three snapshot tiers. Context for the report; no longer the basis of the viability verdict.

tier_projection.description: The observed percentages linearly rescaled onto every tier (factor = current tier's multiplier / target tier's multiplier). Retained as context only - `would_hit_cap` is NOT the viability verdict any more, since a >100% peak on a viable tier is now expected rather than an error.

throttle_projection.description: Per tier, how much TIME that tier would have left the user unable to work (2026-07-26: replaced the old cap-DAY counting, which charged a whole day for a cap hit in the window's last hour, and every remaining day of the week besides). The utilization series is re-expressed as time segments, rescaled per tier, and the portion at/over 100% is summed. The widget reads the flattened copies in verdict.plans rather than this block.

verdict.description: The part the widget's Plan-fit tab actually renders.

plans.description: One entry per canonical tier - the widget's tier grid, one row each. Keys are fixed: adding a tier is a contract change on both sides (Swift iterates a hardcoded list).

recommendation.description: One succinct sentence, always peeking at the adjacent tier: one tier DOWN when the recommended tier fits, one tier UP when the current plan is over tolerance. Rendered verbatim - AppDelegate.planFitTextExtra() measures this live string with NSString boundingRect and grows the fixed panel height so it cannot clip.

data_maturity.description: 'N/90 days collected' caption, with a 'treat as preliminary' qualifier under 7 days. Rendered verbatim, and measured for panel height alongside the recommendation.

throttle_tolerance.description: Surfaced so a consumer can explain what `viable` means without hardcoding the thresholds a second time. The HOURS pair are the real thresholds; the day-equivalents are kept for readers written in the cap-day era.

five_hour_hours_per_month.description: Default 5 - one fully-capped rolling 5h window a month, which is the old 'at most 1 cap-day' intent stated honestly.

seven_day_hours_per_month.description: Default 2 - effectively none, with just enough headroom for a brief end-of-window overrun or bucket-boundary noise. A weekly-cap lockout is treated as disqualifying.

five_hour_days_per_month.description: Day-equivalent of five_hour_hours_per_month, kept only for readers written in the cap-day era. Not the threshold the verdict actually applies.

seven_day_days_per_month.description: Day-equivalent of seven_day_hours_per_month, kept only for readers written in the cap-day era.

totals.description: All-time token totals and API-equivalent cost, per model.

by_model.description: Model id -> totals. Keys are whatever model ids the transcripts carried; not an enum.

pricing_meta.description: Provenance for the pricing chain, which resolves override file -> fetched LiteLLM cache (daily refresh) -> bundled defaults. That fallback order is a project hard constraint.

override_active.description: A user override file was found and used.

cache_present.description: A fetched LiteLLM pricing cache exists on disk.

cache_fetched_at.description: ISO8601 fetch time of that cache; null when absent.

cache_stale.description: The cache exists but is older than the daily refresh interval. NULL when there is no cache to judge - distinct from false, which means a cache exists and is fresh.

bundled_as_of.description: ISO8601 date the hardcoded fallback price table was last checked.

sources_used.description: Sorted set of which layers of the chain actually priced something this run.

assumptions.description: Human-readable caveats the report itself wants stated - including the documented lockout bias: projected 5h lockout is an UPPER BOUND because the series was measured on the current plan, where usage kept accruing past the point a cheaper tier would have cut it off. Weekly is unaffected (its window resets on a fixed schedule either way).

warnings.description: Problems compute() hit and swallowed - unreadable store files, a plan change truncating history, and so on. NOT surfaced anywhere in the UI; see findings F3-4.

spent_usd.description: Sum of already-priced hourly cost buckets inside the current calendar period. A bucket straddling a period boundary can misattribute up to 1 hour of cost.

projected_usd.description: Linear extrapolation (spent / elapsed fraction). NULL in the period's first hour - too little elapsed to extrapolate, same 'no estimate yet' semantics as the widget's usage bars. Under projection_basis 'weekdays' both the elapsed time and the period length count Mon-Fri hours only, and the first-hour suppression is measured in weekday time too (a month opening on a Saturday reports no projection until an hour into Monday).

projected_pct.description: projected/limit as a percentage. Null on the same first-hour rule.

period_start.description: ISO8601 UTC. The boundary is computed in config.json's budget.timezone, DST-safely, then expressed as UTC.

period_end.description: ISO8601 UTC, exclusive. Drives the widget's 'resets in 3d 4h' countdown.

includes_remote.description: True when at least one remote host's usage store was folded into the cost series this run. Display-only.

projection_basis.description: Echo of config.json's budget.projection_basis (defaulted and validated by plan_fit, so an unknown value arrives here as 'calendar'). Tells the widget which clock projected_usd/projected_pct were extrapolated on, for the bar's tooltip. Added after the first release of this block: an OLDER plan_fit.json omits it entirely and the widget reads that as 'calendar', which is what those files were computed with.

value_usd_per_day.description: SUPPRESSED to null (not extrapolated) when under an hour has elapsed since the window's span start - this is what kills the fresh-store explosion where $2 in 10 minutes reads as $288/day, and the 1d window's spike just after 00:00 UTC.

days_covered.description: Integer count of calendar days in the window that have data. Keeps counting even while value_usd_per_day is suppressed, so the maturity captions ('2/7 days') still work.

window_days.description: The window's nominal width. Redundant with the key but read directly by the widget's caption builder.

value_usd.description: Peak spend in that window, 2dp; null with no hourly data.

at.description: ISO8601 UTC hour the peak ended. Unread by the widget.

peak_pct.description: Highest utilization percentage seen. Bucket rows contribute their `max`, which is preserved exactly through every compaction tier - never averaged away - precisely so this stays recoverable from old history.

peak_at.description: ISO8601 UTC of the peak. Unread by the widget.

avg_pct.description: Sample-count-weighted mean (a bucket contributes avg x n). Unread by the widget.

peak_five_hour_pct.description: Observed 5h peak rescaled onto this tier. Over 100% is EXPECTED on a viable tier now; it no longer disqualifies anything.

peak_seven_day_pct.description: Observed weekly peak rescaled onto this tier.

avg_five_hour_pct.description: Observed sample-weighted 5h average rescaled onto this tier.

avg_seven_day_pct.description: Observed sample-weighted weekly average rescaled onto this tier.

would_hit_cap.description: Either projected peak exceeds 100%. LEGACY: this was the viability test before 2026-07-19; it let one monster session permanently veto every cheaper tier. Kept as context.

lockoutStats.description: Lockout accounting for one cap dimension. Normalization is per OBSERVED time, not per calendar time, so stretches where the widget was not collecting do not dilute the rate.

hours_observed.description: Wall-clock the series actually covered for this dimension. Holes wider than LOCKOUT_MAX_SAMPLE_GAP_SECONDS (widget or Mac off) count as neither observed nor locked-out.

days_observed.description: Distinct UTC days touched by observed coverage.

capped_hours.description: Raw observed hours at/over the cap, before normalization.

capped_hours_per_month.description: THE honest unit: capped_hours / hours_observed x a 30-day month. NULL, not 0, when this dimension has no observed coverage at all - 'we cannot say' is deliberately distinct from 'no lockout'.

capped_days_per_month.description: capped_hours_per_month / 24. A display convenience, not a count of days. NULL, not 0, when this dimension has no observed coverage at all - 'we cannot say' is deliberately distinct from 'no lockout'.

throttle_days_per_month.description: Identical value to capped_days_per_month. The name is inherited from the cap-day era and kept so older widget builds keep rendering the column; it now means days' WORTH of lockout, not days on which a cap was touched. NULL, not 0, when this dimension has no observed coverage at all - 'we cannot say' is deliberately distinct from 'no lockout'.

cap_episodes.description: Contiguous runs of capped time. Broken by a segment under the cap, or by a coverage gap too long to bridge - a SHORT collection gap between two capped segments is missing data, not a recovery.

median_episode_hours.description: Median episode length - 'how long am I stuck when it happens'. Null with no episodes.

longest_episode_hours.description: Worst single episode. Emitted but never read by the widget; see findings F3-3.

days_with_cap.description: Distinct UTC days touched by any lockout. This IS the old cap-day count, demoted to context.

median_throttle_peak_pct.description: Median projected peak across capped segments: how deep into the cap a typical lockout went.

anyCapStats.description: lockoutStats for EITHER cap, plus the split that says which cap is binding. This is a UNION, not a sum: both caps climb while you work, so within a segment both crossings sit at its busy end (a nested-interval model - union = max(frac_5h, frac_7d), overlap = min(...)). Adding the dimensions double-counts heavily; on live data one tier read 87h + 644h but only 677h union.

hours_observed.description: Wall-clock the series actually covered for this dimension. Holes wider than LOCKOUT_MAX_SAMPLE_GAP_SECONDS (widget or Mac off) count as neither observed nor locked-out.

days_observed.description: Distinct UTC days touched by observed coverage.

capped_hours.description: Raw observed hours at/over the cap, before normalization.

capped_hours_per_month.description: NULL, not 0, when this dimension has no observed coverage at all - 'we cannot say' is deliberately distinct from 'no lockout'.

capped_days_per_month.description: NULL, not 0, when this dimension has no observed coverage at all - 'we cannot say' is deliberately distinct from 'no lockout'.

throttle_days_per_month.description: NULL, not 0, when this dimension has no observed coverage at all - 'we cannot say' is deliberately distinct from 'no lockout'.

cap_episodes.description: Contiguous runs of capped time. Broken by a segment under the cap, or by a coverage gap too long to bridge - a SHORT collection gap between two capped segments is missing data, not a recovery.

median_episode_hours.description: Median episode length - 'how long am I stuck when it happens'. Null with no episodes.

longest_episode_hours.description: Worst single episode. Emitted but never read by the widget; see findings F3-3.

days_with_cap.description: Distinct UTC days touched by any lockout. This IS the old cap-day count, demoted to context.

median_throttle_peak_pct.description: Median projected peak across capped segments: how deep into the cap a typical lockout went.

overlap_hours.description: Time BOTH caps were hit, under the nested-interval model.

five_hour_only_hours.description: Lockout attributable to the 5h cap alone. Feeds the recommendation's '(5h cap)' tag.

seven_day_only_hours.description: Lockout attributable to the weekly cap alone. Feeds the '(weekly cap)' tag.

planVerdict.description: One row of the widget's tier grid: throttle_projection flattened, plus pricing. Every field here is a copy of something in throttle_projection - the flattening exists so the widget never has to walk that nested block.

api_equiv_ratio.description: monthly_run_rate / price - 'this tier is worth N x its price at your usage'. Rendered as the grid's 'x API' column. Null with no run rate.

projected_peak_7d_util.description: All-time projected weekly peak. Context only now.

projected_peak_5h_util.description: All-time projected 5h peak. Context only now.

capped_hours_5h_per_month.description: Projected hours/month locked out by the 5h cap on this tier. UPPER BOUND: the series was measured on the current plan, where usage kept accruing past the point a cheaper tier would have cut it off.

capped_hours_7d_per_month.description: Projected hours/month locked out by the weekly cap on this tier. Unbiased - the weekly window resets on a fixed schedule either way.

capped_hours_any_per_month.description: The union figure - what you would actually lose. Leads the grid's 'Capped/mo' cell.

median_lockout_any_hours.description: Median length of a single lockout from either cap - 'how long am I stuck when it happens'. Shown in the tier-grid tooltip.

throttle_days_5h_per_month.description: Day-equivalent. Name predates the hours switch; the widget uses it as the fallback when capped_hours_* is absent (older daemon).

throttle_days_7d_per_month.description: Day-equivalent of capped_hours_7d_per_month. Same legacy naming as the 5h field.

median_lockout_5h_hours.description: Median length of a single 5h-cap lockout. Shown in the tier-grid tooltip.

median_lockout_7d_hours.description: Median length of a single weekly-cap lockout. Shown in the tier-grid tooltip.

median_throttle_peak_5h_pct.description: Median projected 5h peak across capped segments - how deep into the cap a typical lockout went. Shown in the tooltip as 'usage while capped peaks near N%'.

median_throttle_peak_7d_pct.description: Median projected weekly peak across capped segments.

price_delta_vs_current_usd.description: price_usd minus the current plan's price. Negative = a saving. Drives the recommendation's phrasing.

viable.description: Within BOTH hour tolerances (verdict.throttle_tolerance). Authoritative: TierVerdict.isFlagged trusts it whenever any throttle field is present, because a >100% projected peak on a viable tier is now expected. WARNING: the Swift decoder defaults a missing `viable` to TRUE - it fails open. See findings F3-2.

has_peak_data.description: At least one projected peak was computable. When no tier has peak data the recommendation says so instead of guessing.

input.description: All-time uncached input tokens attributed to this model.

cache_write.description: All-time cache-creation tokens (priced differently from plain input).

cache_read.description: All-time cache-read tokens (the cheapest class; usually the largest count).

web_searches.description: All-time server-side web search calls, which are priced per call rather than per token.

messages.description: Deduped message count - transcripts repeat a message under (message.id, requestId), so only the first occurrence is folded in.

cost_usd.description: API-equivalent cost of the above at the resolved rates, 2dp. This - not any subscription price - is what the tier comparison ratios divide by.

pricing_sources.description: Which layers of the pricing chain priced this model.
